title: EngineCommand planning wire representation
description: Proposed v0.2 semantic schema. Native implementation uses bounded typed commands, not JSON parsing in the audio callback. Only the trusted local command bridge may construct commands. origin and automationRef are not model-granted authority. Automation events are installed through atomic batch admission and carry an engine-issued, engine-owned revision checked immediately before execution. Final command payload schemas and ABI are selected after G1.

origin.description: Assigned by the trusted bridge. A model response cannot select origin or elevate its authority.

automationRef.description: Non-null only for events from an engine-admitted batch. Issued by the engine and held in trusted native/controller state; never generated by or exposed as an authority-bearing model field.

engineInstanceId.description: Engine-created instance identity assigned off-thread at initialization. The trusted bridge attaches it; stale commands and acknowledgements from an earlier engine instance are rejected.

uint64.description: Decimal uint64; native validator also enforces the maximum value and current-state equality.

automationRef.description: Engine-owned register identity/revision, not a bearer capability or user approval. Bound to engine instance, stream epoch, affected deck/control generations and accepted plan. Cancel/invalidation advances the revision. Never reuse a live identity or resurrect it after restart.

controlRevision.description: Revision of superseding external/manual control changes. Ordinary event writes within this accepted plan do not increment this guard and invalidate themselves.

admitAutomationBatch.description: References an immutable, preallocated batch constructed by the trusted local planner after user/source checks. Engine verifies handle ownership, accepted plan identity, all unique scope bindings, timing and total capacity before making any event runnable. On any rejection, install zero events and invalidate/discard all staged siblings. The actual runtime capacity may be lower than this planning ceiling. Success acknowledgement supplies the engine-issued automationRef attached internally to every event.

cancelAutomation.description: Cancellation uses reserved bounded control capacity or an equivalent engine-owned invalidation path; normal scheduling queue saturation cannot drop Stop Automation. At the engine control boundary, invalidate before later affected events. ALL cancels the current session automation registry; ONE targets its engine-issued ID. A stale caller revision must not prevent cancelling the current instance of that ID.

automationAcknowledgement.description: Semantic acknowledgement contract, carried outside the render callback. ADMITTED means the entire plan was installed; REJECTED means zero events became runnable. CANCELLED/ALREADY_INACTIVE report the execution barrier after which no event under the invalidated token can run. Already-heard audio is not reversed. Acknowledgement journaling is off-thread.

$comment: Normative semantic checks: automation events are never admitted individually. The engine checks automation identity/revision, stream epoch and affected deck/control guards immediately before each event; scheduling-time validation alone is insufficient. At a shared control boundary, manual takeover/cancellation invalidation precedes remaining affected due events. Invalidating one plan rejects all pending siblings. Direct manual input cancels affected automation before applying its value; cancellation does not reset audible parameters. Admission and cancellation are idempotent by requestSequenceId within engine instance; duplicate IDs with changed payload are rejected, completed outcomes replayed without mutation. App restart discards queued events and tokens. Registry acknowledgements must distinguish accepted, applied and cancelled; no callback file/database I/O. MASTER and SAMPLER guards refer to their engine-owned scope generations. Ordinary non-automation payloads remain draft and need command-specific G1 schemas. engineInstanceId is validated before sequence/idempotency resolution, preventing old-instance ID/epoch reuse from accepting delayed commands. Superseding control revisions advance for external/manual changes, not for the active plan applying its own accepted values.
